reasoning: Recent polling in North Carolina’s 2026 U.S. Senate race consistently shows Democrat Roy Cooper leading Republican Michael Whatley by mid‑single to low‑double digits, even though the state’s underlying Cook PVI is slightly Republican (R+1). Within the last 45 days, general‑election Senate polls from Fox News/Beacon & Shaw and Elon University/YouGov, aggregated by outlets like The New York Times and The Hill, all show Cooper ahead by between 4 and 11 points, with the most recent high‑quality polls clustering around a Cooper lead of roughly 9–11 points. I found no state‑specific 2026 presidential general‑election polling for North Carolina in this window, so the current measurable margin applies to the Senate race only.

sources.name: Fox News / Beacon Research & Shaw Company
sources.details: Fox News/Beacon Research & Shaw Company poll of 1,005 registered North Carolina voters finds Roy Cooper leading Michael Whatley 53% to 44% in the 2026 U.S. Senate race (Cooper +9).

sources.name: Elon University Poll / YouGov
sources.details: Elon University poll conducted with YouGov finds among likely North Carolina voters Roy Cooper at 53% and Michael Whatley at 42% in the U.S. Senate race (Cooper +11).

sources.name: Change Research (reported by The New York Times)
sources.details: Change Research poll summarized by The New York Times shows Roy Cooper leading Michael Whatley 50% to 41% in the North Carolina U.S. Senate race (Cooper +9).

sources.name: Elon University/YouGov (reported by The New York Times)
sources.details: New York Times polling overview lists Elon University/YouGov survey of North Carolina U.S. Senate race with Cooper ahead of Whatley 53% to 42% among likely voters (Cooper +11).

sources.name: Public Policy Polling (reported by Roll Call)
sources.details: Public Policy Polling survey cited by Roll Call finds Roy Cooper leading Michael Whatley 48% to 44% in the North Carolina Senate race (Cooper +4).

sources.name: The Hill (Fox News/Beacon & Shaw polling)
sources.details: The Hill’s write‑up of the Fox News poll reports Cooper preferred by 53% of registered North Carolina voters versus 44% for Whatley in the U.S. Senate race (Cooper +9).

sources.name: The Hill (Elon University/YouGov polling)
sources.details: The Hill’s coverage of the Elon University poll notes that among likely North Carolina voters, Cooper receives 53% support to Whatley’s 42% in the Senate race (Cooper +11).

sources.name: Roll Call (Public Policy Polling)
sources.details: Roll Call describes a Public Policy Polling survey finding Cooper at 48% and Whatley at 44% in the North Carolina Senate contest (Cooper +4).

sources.name: ABC11 (Fox News/Beacon & Shaw polling)
sources.details: ABC11/WTVD story on the Fox News survey reports Cooper leading Whatley 53% to 44% among registered North Carolina voters (Cooper +9) in the Senate race.

sources.name: Citizen-Times (Catawba College study)
sources.details: Catawba College study, as summarized by Citizen-Times, reports approval ratings for North Carolina’s U.S. Senate candidates—Cooper at 48% and Whatley at 34%—but does not provide a direct vote-choice margin.

sources.name: Cook Political Report PVI (as summarized by Wikipedia)
sources.details: Cook Partisan Voting Index lists North Carolina’s statewide PVI as R+1, indicating the state voted one percentage point more Republican than the nation as a whole in recent presidential elections.
